subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 52-year-old man reports a 6-month history of progressive curvature of his penis during erections, associated with pain and difficulty achieving penetration. He has no history of sexually transmitted infection or urethral discharge. Physical examination reveals a palpable, firm plaque along the dorsal aspect of the penile shaft. He is distressed by the cosmetic and functional changes.
question: Which of the following best explains the underlying cause of this patient's condition?

options.text: Rupture of the tunica albuginea after forced bending of an erect penis (penile fracture)
Fibrous plaque within the tunica albuginea from repeated minor trauma during intercourse (Peyronie disease)
Accumulation of serous fluid within the tunica vaginalis (hydrocele)
Dilated veins of the pampiniform plexus (varicocele)
Infection of the epididymis by Chlamydia trachomatis (epididymitis)

explanation_correct: Peyronie disease is characterized by abnormal curvature of the penis due to a fibrous plaque within the tunica albuginea, arising from repeated minor trauma during intercourse. The plaque causes pain, anxiety, and erectile dysfunction. Treatment with collagenase injections or surgical repair is considered once the curvature stabilizes. This is distinct from penile fracture, which is an acute rupture of the tunica albuginea from forced bending.

explanation_incorrect.A: Penile fracture is an acute rupture of the tunica albuginea after forced bending of an erect penis, presenting with sudden pain and swelling, not a chronic progressive curvature with a plaque.
explanation_incorrect.C: A hydrocele is a serous fluid collection within the tunica vaginalis that transilluminates and causes scrotal rather than penile swelling.
explanation_incorrect.D: A varicocele is dilation of the pampiniform plexus (a bag of worms) in the scrotum and does not cause penile curvature.
explanation_incorrect.E: Epididymitis presents with posterior testicular pain and a positive Prehn sign from infection, not a firm penile shaft plaque.

educationalObjective: Peyronie disease is a fibrotic plaque in the tunica albuginea causing painful penile curvature after repeated minor trauma, distinct from acute penile fracture.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 24-year-old man with sickle cell disease presents to the emergency department with a painful erection that has persisted for 6 hours. He reports no sexual arousal and the erection is not relieved by orgasm. Physical examination shows a rigid, tender penis. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 8 g/dL with sickled erythrocytes on smear.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this patient's condition and the most appropriate immediate management?

options.text: Increased arterial inflow from sildenafil; treat with additional sildenafil
Thrombosis of the dorsal penile artery; treat with systemic anticoagulation alone
Sickled erythrocytes obstructing venous drainage of the corpus cavernosum; perform corporal aspiration and intracavernosal phenylephrine
Fibrous plaque contraction within the tunica albuginea; inject collagenase
Rupture of the tunica albuginea; perform immediate surgical repair of the fracture

explanation_correct: Ischemic priapism is a painful sustained erection lasting longer than 4 hours, here caused by sickle cell disease in which sickled RBCs block venous drainage of the corpus cavernosum vascular channels, trapping deoxygenated blood. Medications such as sildenafil and trazodone are also associated. It is a urologic emergency requiring immediate corporal aspiration, intracavernosal phenylephrine, or surgical decompression to prevent ischemic damage.

explanation_incorrect.A: Sildenafil can precipitate priapism by enhancing erection, but giving more PDE-5 inhibitor would worsen the condition rather than relieve it.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ischemic priapism is a failure of venous outflow, not arterial thrombosis; anticoagulation alone does not emergently decompress the corpora.
explanation_incorrect.D: A fibrous tunica plaque causes Peyronie disease with curvature, not an acute painful sustained erection; collagenase is not the treatment here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tunica albuginea rupture is penile fracture from forced bending, presenting with immediate detumescence and swelling, not a sustained rigid erection.

educationalObjective: Ischemic priapism is a painful erection over 4 hours from impaired venous drainage (eg, sickle cell disease), managed emergently with corporal aspiration and intracavernosal phenylephrine.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 58-year-old uncircumcised man is evaluated for a well-demarcated, bright red, velvety plaque on the glans penis that has been slowly enlarging for several months. Biopsy confirms carcinoma in situ. HPV-16 DNA is detected in the lesion.
question: Which of the following is the correct diagnosis for this in situ lesion?

options.text: Erythroplasia of Queyrat
Bowen disease
Bowenoid papulosis
Peyronie disease
Condyloma acuminatum

explanation_correct: Erythroplasia of Queyrat is carcinoma in situ of the glans penis, presenting as an erythroplakia (a red plaque). It, along with Bowen disease and Bowenoid papulosis, is a precursor to penile squamous cell carcinoma, the most common penile cancer. Risk factors include being uncircumcised and HPV-16 infection.

explanation_incorrect.B: Bowen disease is carcinoma in situ of the penile shaft, presenting as leukoplakia (a white plaque), not a red glans lesion.
explanation_incorrect.C: Bowenoid papulosis presents as reddish papules of unclear malignant potential rather than a single velvety red plaque on the glans.
explanation_incorrect.D: Peyronie disease is a fibrous tunica albuginea plaque causing curvature, not a premalignant epithelial lesion.
explanation_incorrect.E: Condyloma acuminatum is a benign HPV-related wart, not carcinoma in situ.

educationalObjective: Erythroplasia of Queyrat is carcinoma in situ of the glans (red plaque), a precursor to HPV-16-associated penile squamous cell carcinoma.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 31-year-old man presents to the emergency department after his erect penis was forcibly bent during intercourse. He heard an audible pop, experienced immediate severe pain with rapid detumescence, and developed progressive swelling and leftward deviation of the penis. The urology team suspects penile fracture.
question: Which of the following best distinguishes this condition from Peyronie disease?

options.text: Peyronie disease results from forced bending of an erect penis, whereas this condition results from repeated minor trauma
Penile fracture produces a chronic fibrous plaque, whereas Peyronie disease produces an acute hematoma
Peyronie disease requires emergent surgical decompression, whereas penile fracture is managed with collagenase injections
Penile fracture is an acute rupture of the tunica albuginea after forced bending, whereas Peyronie disease is a fibrous plaque from repeated minor trauma causing curvature
Both conditions are caused by sickled RBCs obstructing venous drainage of the corpus cavernosum

explanation_correct: Penile fracture is the acute rupture of the tunica albuginea due to forced bending of an erect penis, producing an audible pop, immediate detumescence, pain, and swelling, and often requiring urgent surgical repair. Peyronie disease is a chronic fibrous plaque within the tunica albuginea from repeated minor trauma, causing progressive curvature, pain, and erectile dysfunction; collagenase or surgery is considered once curvature stabilizes. They involve the same layer but differ in acuity and mechanism.

explanation_incorrect.A: This reverses the mechanisms; Peyronie disease follows repeated minor trauma, while fracture follows acute forced bending.
explanation_incorrect.B: It is Peyronie disease that produces a chronic fibrous plaque, whereas penile fracture produces an acute hematoma and swelling.
explanation_incorrect.C: Penile fracture may need urgent repair; collagenase injections are used for stable Peyronie disease, not the reverse.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sickled RBCs obstructing venous outflow cause ischemic priapism, not penile fracture or Peyronie disease.

educationalObjective: Penile fracture is acute tunica albuginea rupture from forced bending, whereas Peyronie disease is a chronic fibrotic plaque from repeated minor trauma.
